versions.text: Verify that brake control power is equal and proportional to brake pedal movement. Comm’l Doc: SAE ARP-1070. DoD/MIL Doc: JSSG-2009 Appendix A: A.3.4.1.4.4.1/A.4.4.1.4.4.1 Braking Control Interface; MIL-B-8584 Design of Brake Systems

Criterion: Verify that brake control power is equal and proportional to brake input command. Standard: To produce repeatable and predictable braking actuation forces, input commands are proportional to output commands. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include tests and demonstrations. Laboratory testing verifies that input commands and output braking forces are proportional as designed and brake release and running clearances are maintained. Air vehicle checkout verifies that air vehicle system operation and integration matches that which was tested. Ground and flight braking tests verify performance. References: JSSG-2009: A.3.4.1.4.4.1, A.4.4.1.4.4.1 Braking Control Interface MIL-B-8584 SAE ARP1070

Standard: Right and left brakes are separately actuated and the flight crew and autonomous system brake input commands are proportional to brake control torque output allowing directional control of air vehicle. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review of brake control schematic verifies independent control of left and right brakes are provided.
(2) Review of the brake pedal input (deflection and force) versus brake pressure or torque curve shows flight crew brake inputs are proportional to brake pressure or torque output. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct lab testing to verify that input commands and output braking pressures or torques are proportional as designed.
  (2) Ground test: Conduct ground testing to verify the air vehicle system operation and integration is within acceptable limits of lab testing results.
